summary: Two unrelated things the group talks about on the same day are now two notes. Until this, anything the background pass wrote for a day it already had a note for was folded into that note, whatever it was about.
details: The note-candidates pass matched a proposed note to a standing one on the ANCHOR DATE alone. Measured 2026-09-13: that arm had fired exactly twice since the tier shipped and both times it merged two genuinely different occasions — a sign-up deadline and a games thread that shared nothing but the calendar day, and a gathering note overwritten forty minutes later by an unrelated room's pass. Notes are per-group, so every room in a group wrote onto whichever note shared the date (issue #228).

The pass is now asked which entry it is updating, and answers with that entry's title exactly as its notebook shows it. Code resolves the title and nothing else: one match revises, nothing named creates, and a title that answers to more than one entry creates rather than guessing which was meant — a duplicate is something the group can see and fix, appending to the wrong entry is not. The date is back to meaning only when the thing happens, which is what schedules the note's own follow-up.

The pass could already see the notebook and was already told not to duplicate what was in it; its answer was being discarded. What changed is that a wrong answer is now recoverable: since the first half of this issue a revision appends rather than replaces, so the worst case is an entry that carries two threads and the group can still read both.

A proposal whose empty `updates` field used to throw the whole note away is now read as "this is new" — an empty string was one of the commonest ways the pass said "not applicable", and the note it came with was being discarded silently.
limitations: Nothing merges two entries that turn out to describe the same thing. The background curator retires; its merge half was removed in September, and the create path's date match — which was what handled duplicates where they first appeared — is what this change deletes. A duplicate stands until it retires on its own date like any other entry, and shows in the notebook until then. Bounded in time, not in number; tracked as issue #236, with the rate now readable rather than assumed.

Two arrangements on one date that the pass proposes WITHOUT naming any people for either are still handled as one — the staging table that queues proposals keys on the date and the people, and with no people named the two collide before the new rule is reached. The dropped proposal is now counted and logged rather than vanishing silently (issue #235).

The instruction that routes around that collision — name the people when one batch holds two entries on one date — only reaches a single batch. Two rooms of one group proposing on the same date in separate passes cannot see each other, and two entries about the same group of people on one date are not separated by naming them either.

Resolution is by exact title, so an entry whose title the pass mistypes reads as new and is written as a second entry. That case is now counted separately from an ordinary new entry, so how often it happens can be read rather than guessed.
